title: Microsoft Teams: keypad consent for recording and transcription in one-to-one PSTN calls
summary: The briefing accurately describes the planned keypad consent experience and the existing calling-policy controls. It distinguishes automatic rollout from the disabled-by-default consent setting, and explicitly reports Microsoft's conflicting documentation about consent auditing and parameter availability.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The keypad extension reaches the users covered by existing enabled consent policies without new configuration.
claims.quote: No new policy configuration is required if your existing explicit consent configuration meets your organization's requirements.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the planned one-to-one PSTN keypad prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN one to one explicit consent keypad press 1 2 policy switch licensing Teams Phone recording consent. Opened call-recording-transcription-captions and participant-agreement-recording-transcription; keypad results describe Audio Conferencing, not this planned 1:1 change.

claims.claim: The current call-recording documentation describes a Yes or No consent prompt for call participants.
claims.quote: When a participant decides to un-mute, turn on their camera, or share content, they’re asked to respond 'Yes' or 'No' to consent to be included in the recording and transcription.

claims.claim: The calling-policy ExplicitRecordingConsent parameter governs both one-to-one VoIP and PSTN calls.
claims.quote: This parameter manages recording consent for Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN calls.

claims.claim: The meeting-consent Learn page currently lists PSTN endpoints in one-to-one calls as auto-consented.
claims.quote: The following user types are auto consented for recording and transcription without any participant interaction. ... PSTN endpoints in 1:1 calls

claims.claim: Learn says the consent choice for each call participant is visible to an administrator.
claims.quote: The consent choice for each participant is visible by the admin and is included in the Purview audit log for the call.

Opened call-recording-transcription-captions, participant-agreement-recording-transcription and audit-log-activities; none specifically documents the planned 1:1 PSTN keypad-choice audit mapping.

claims.claim: The notice describes phone-keypad responses and describes no sign-in step.
claims.quote: PSTN participants will hear an audio prompt when recording or transcription starts and can use their phone keypad to consent or decline.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not separately explain call-queue applicability for the planned keypad extension.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN keypad consent audit CallParticipantDetail call queue ExplicitRecordingConsent. Opened call-recording-transcription-captions and read MC1530950; current explicit consent excludes call queues, but neither describes a call-queue case for the future keypad extension.

claims.claim: The planned change describes participant consent interactions rather than autonomous actions.
claims.quote: They can use their phone keypad to consent or decline. Participants who decline can remain in the call but stay muted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[0].scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Calling policies apply to users, so different assigned consent settings can give users different behaviour.
claims.quote: You can assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment (if supported for the policy type), or to a group that the users are members of (if supported for the policy type).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: This capability uses the existing explicit consent setting in Teams calling policies. It does not introduce a new admin policy setting.

claims.claim: The calling-policies Learn page describes the consent setting without naming a licence for it.
claims.quote: Require participant agreement for recording and transcription - When this is on, participants must agree to be recorded and transcribed.

claims.where: controls[1]; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No separately documented PSTN-only or keypad-only consent switch exists on the admin UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN only keypad explicit recording consent switch Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy. Opened teams-calling-policy, call-recording-transcription-captions and Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; only the shared ExplicitRecordingConsent control was documented, matching MC1530950's no-new-setting statement.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The consent setting is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Require participant agreement for recording and transcription.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit. ... Require participant agreement for recording and transcription

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell documents Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent <string>, subject to the explicitly reported release warning.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy ... [-Identity] <string> ... [-ExplicitRecordingConsent <string>] ... This setting controls whether users must provide or obtain explicit consent before recording a 1:1 PSTN or Teams call.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference marks ExplicitRecordingConsent as not yet released, in conflict with descriptions of an existing setting elsewhere.
claims.quote: This feature has not been released yet and will have no changes if it is enabled or disabled.

claims.claim: The recording permission control is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Cloud recording for calling.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit. ... Turn Cloud recording for calling to On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true enables call recording for the global policy.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables call recording for the global policy: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true

claims.claim: The transcription permission control is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. ... Select the policy you want to modify. ... Turn Transcription to On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true enables transcription for the global policy.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables transcription for the global policy: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true

claims.where: controls[4].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Audit searches are configured in Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search, using Activities - friendly names and a date range, then Search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable: ... Activities - friendly names ... Select Search to start your search job.

claims.where: controls[4].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell supports Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start date> -EndDate <end date> -Operations CallParticipantDetail for the named operation, with the audit-source disagreement explicitly reported.
claims.quote: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -EndDate <ExDateTime> -StartDate <ExDateTime> ... [-Operations <String[]>] ... The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation. ... For a list of the available values for this parameter, see Audited activities.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout; controls[4].note
claims.claim: CallParticipantDetail is the operation for Added information about call participants; the audit reference qualifies that recorded or transcribed calls are included in MeetingParticipantDetail.
claims.quote: Added information about call participants ... CallParticipantDetail ... Calls that are recorded or transcribed are included in MeetingParticipantDetail.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout; controls[4].note
claims.claim: The call-recording page directs administrators to Added information about call participants for consent data, notwithstanding the separate audit-reference qualification reported by the briefing.
claims.quote: You can view consent data using the Added information about call participants filter in the Teams calling audit logs in Purview.

claims.claim: Audio Conferencing and group-call consent are managed by Teams meeting policy rather than the calling-policy parameter.
claims.quote: This parameter manages recording consent for Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN calls. Audio conferencing and group calls are managed by Teams Meeting Policy.
